$comment: L2 gloss layer for the ingested Missouri clauses: plain-language 'what this means' rewrites at two reading levels (src/schema/gloss.ts). Batch-drafted, then frozen; reviewed_by records the initial editorial pass — a named human reviewer should confirm each gloss against the clause text before classroom use. Reading levels are enforced by scripts/check-reading-level.mjs against READING_LEVEL_BANDS. A gloss explains only its own clause — it never imports rules from neighboring sections.

glosses.grade_5: The people keep two powers for themselves. They can write a new law and put it to a vote. They can also vote yes or no on a law the lawmakers passed.
glosses.grade_8: The people keep two powers. By initiative, they can propose a law or an amendment and pass it at the ballot. By referendum, they can approve or reject a law the general assembly passed.

glosses.grade_5: When a judge's job opens up, a special group picks three people who could do it. The governor must choose one of those three.
glosses.grade_8: When a judge's seat on certain courts opens up, a nonpartisan commission picks three candidates. The governor must appoint one of the three.

glosses.grade_5: You can vote in Missouri if you are a citizen of the United States, you are 18 or older, and you live here. The section also says when someone cannot vote.
glosses.grade_8: Voters must be United States citizens, at least eighteen, and residents of Missouri and their district. The section also lists times when a person cannot vote, such as while serving a felony sentence.

glosses.grade_5: Missouri says learning keeps people free. So the state must run free public schools that anyone up to age 21 can attend.
glosses.grade_8: An educated public protects everyone’s rights and freedom. So the constitution requires the state to establish and maintain free public schools, open to everyone up to age twenty-one.
